question: Should outbound recovery keep ambiguous entries pending with backoff when no reconciliation-capable adapter is available, instead of moving them to failed?
rationale: Both states are defensible: pending preserves future reconciliation, while terminal failed gives operators an explicit fail-closed state; tests cannot choose that product/operations tradeoff.

options.title: Accept Recoverable Pending
options.body: Merge after the no-op pacing blocker is fixed if maintainers want no-adapter ambiguous entries to remain recoverable until adapter reconciliation ships.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed State
options.body: Close or pause this PR and keep current main's terminal failed behavior until the broader delivery ledger is designed.

options.title: Require Operator Surface First
options.body: Ask for a companion UI, doctor, or API surface before changing ambiguous entries to remain pending longer.

recommendation.title: Accept Recoverable Pending
recommendation.body: Merge after the no-op pacing blocker is fixed if maintainers want no-adapter ambiguous entries to remain recoverable until adapter reconciliation ships.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merge history shows steipete owned the latest outbound recovery merge decisions and is the best available owner for the pending-vs-failed operator tradeoff.
